title: Peak season fulfillment: An October–December execution checklist
summary: Keep peak season fulfillment on track from October through December. Get practical steps for inventory, partner accountability, and holiday shipping deadlines.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


- In October, confirm inventory, test promo workflows, and align on partner capacity and SLAs.
- Before November promotions, recheck stock, order priorities, and carrier pickups against updated forecasts.
- During peak volume, daily monitor aging orders, stock shortages, and shipping exceptions with assigned owners.
- Flowspace combines software visibility and hands-on support to keep peak and year-round orders moving smoothly.


A promotion takes off. A replenishment shipment arrives late. Orders pile up faster than expected. Peak season fulfillment depends on how quickly your team spots these changes and responds.


From October through December, keep your operating plan current and stay closely aligned with your fulfillment partner. Both teams should know what needs attention, who can make decisions, and when to escalate.


Use this checklist to guide those conversations. Each stage builds on the last: inventory checks, performance monitoring, and customer communication should continue throughout the season.


## October: Validate your fulfillment plan and close the gaps


Start by checking whether your holiday fulfillment plan still matches what you expect to sell—and what your operation can handle.


### What your brand should do


- **Refresh the forecast:** Share expected orders by day, promoted SKUs, units per order, and any bundles or special packing requirements. Monthly totals can hide a sharp promotional spike.
- **Confirm when inventory will be ready to fulfill:** Inventory arriving at the warehouse may still need to be checked, recorded, and put away before it’s available to fulfill orders. Confirm that timeline with your partner.
- **Test promotional workflows:** Place test orders for bundles, gifts with purchase, subscriptions, and any new sales channels. Check that orders, inventory updates, and tracking information move correctly between systems.
- **Check supplies and backup options:** Confirm packaging availability, which carrier services are already configured, and rate shopping capabilities.


For example, a holiday gift set may require several items, an insert, and a different carton. Your partner needs that detail to plan labor and supplies accurately.


### What your fulfillment partner should be doing


Your partner should compare the forecast with available capacity, flag constraints, and confirm receiving and shipping schedules.


Review your[service-level agreements (SLAs)](https://flow.space/blog/software-service-slas) —the agreed service commitments—and confirm whether any peak conditions affect processing timelines, order cutoffs, or volume limits. Agree on an escalation contact and the information both teams need when something goes wrong.


**Ask your partner:** “Where could our plan exceed capacity, and what should we adjust now?”


## Early November: Confirm readiness for promotional spikes


Use early November to check the details behind your largest promotions. Update the plan with what October’s orders have already taught you.


### What your brand should do


- **Recheck promoted products:** Confirm available stock, expected replenishment, and the inventory needed to support each campaign.
- **Coordinate sales channels:** If your brand is[omnichannel](https://flow.space/blog/omnichannel-fulfillment-b2b-retail) , account for subscription or[subscription box](https://flow.space/blog/subscription-box-fulfillment) orders, marketplace demand, and retail commitments before allocating stock to a DTC promotion.
- **Communicate changes early:** An extended sale, deeper discount, or new bundle can change both order volume and the work required to fulfill it.
- **Agree on decision rules:** Decide who can pause a promotion, approve extra shipping costs, or change order priorities.


If a promoted SKU runs low, marketing should know while there’s still time to change the offer. Set that communication path before the campaign launches.


### What your fulfillment partner should be doing


Your partner should confirm that inventory, staffing, packing workflows, and carrier pickups support the latest forecast. Ask how the team will handle a surge above expected volume and when it will alert you that shipping commitments are at risk.


Agree on a regular check-in schedule, with more frequent updates during your busiest days.


**Ask your partner:** “What could prevent promotional orders from shipping within our agreed timelines?”


## Late November: Manage peak season fulfillment in real time


During major promotions, keep reviews short and focused on decisions. A dashboard is useful when it helps someone take action.


### What your brand should do


Review these signals with your fulfillment partner:


Peak season monitoring checklist


What to monitor What to do with it


Orders versus forecast Reassess capacity and promotional plans if demand changes sharply.


Available inventory for promoted SKUs Adjust offers or replenishment priorities before products sell out.


Unshipped orders approaching their deadlines Identify the cause and assign an owner to resolve it.


Carrier handoffs and shipment exceptions Investigate pickup issues or stalled shipments and update affected customers.


Cost per order Check whether upgrades, split shipments, or packaging changes are increasing spend.


Look beyond the overall on-time shipping percentage. Identify which orders are waiting, how long they’ve been waiting, and what is blocking them.


Keep fulfillment performance and carrier delivery performance separate in your reviews. An order leaving the warehouse on time can still encounter a transit delay; each issue requires a different response.


For a closer look at seasonal carrier charges, see Flowspace’s guide to[2026 peak season surcharges](https://flow.space/blog/peak-shipping-season) .


### **What your fulfillment partner should be doing**


Your partner should surface orders at risk of missing agreed service levels, explain the cause, provide a recovery plan, and proactively resolve it. Each issue needs an owner, a next action, and a time for the next update.


Make those updates specific enough for your team to act. “Inventory discrepancy affecting these orders; count underway; next update at 2 p.m.” is more useful than “We’re looking into it.”


**Ask your partner:** “Which orders are at risk today, and what action is underway?”


## December: Protect delivery promises and the customer experience


As delivery windows tighten, review what customers see alongside what your operation can deliver. Build the deadline plan earlier in the season, then adjust it as actual performance changes.


### Set holiday shipping deadlines your operation can support


**Your customer’s order deadline must account for both fulfillment processing and carrier transit time.**


Work backward from the intended arrival date, allowing for:


- The carrier service and destination
- Warehouse processing time and daily order cutoffs
- Pickup schedules, weekends, and holiday closures
- A reasonable buffer based on current performance


Check the latest[USPS holiday shipping deadlines](https://www.usps.com/holiday/holiday-shipping-dates.htm) ,[FedEx last days to ship](https://www.fedex.com/en-us/holiday/last-days-to-ship.html) , and UPS holiday operating guidance. Carrier recommendations and schedules vary by service and destination.


For example, if a carrier recommends shipping by a Thursday and your warehouse needs two business days to process an order, your customer-facing deadline must fall earlier. Confirm the exact cutoff and pickup timing with your partner before publishing it.


### What your brand should do


Keep holiday shipping messages consistent across product pages, checkout, promotional emails, and customer support.


As deadlines approach, remove outdated arrival promises and clearly explain remaining options. Decide when a shipping upgrade is appropriate, who approves the cost, and whether it can still meet the customer’s needs.


Make returns instructions easy to find, including eligibility, the return window, and expected refund timing.


### What your fulfillment partner should be doing


Your partner should provide current processing and pickup guidance, flag orders at risk, and explain available shipping alternatives. A faster carrier service only helps if the order can be processed and handed off in time.


The team should also maintain visibility into returns receiving and inspection so your support team can give customers accurate updates.


**Ask your partner:** “When should we adjust order deadlines, delivery messaging, or shipping services?”


## After peak: Turn performance into your next action plan


Schedule a review while the details are still fresh. Compare forecast and actual volume, cost per order, inventory availability, shipping performance, returns processing, and customer-service issues.


Ask your fulfillment partner to explain recurring service misses and recommend fixes. Identify whether each problem came from forecasting, inventory, warehouse execution, system issues, or transportation.


Leave with a short action list, an owner for each change, and a completion date. Apply those lessons before your next promotion.

## Peak season fulfillment FAQs


### What should brands prioritize during peak season fulfillment?


Prioritize available inventory, fulfillment capacity, orders approaching shipping deadlines, and accurate customer communication. Update forecasts as demand changes and assign clear owners for issues that could delay orders.


### What should a fulfillment partner do during peak season?


A fulfillment partner should align capacity with the agreed forecast, track service commitments, flag inventory and order risks, and resolve exceptions. When delays occur, the partner should explain which orders are affected, what action is underway, and when to expect an update.


### How should brands set holiday shipping deadlines?


Work backward from the intended delivery date using carrier transit estimates, warehouse processing time, order cutoffs, and pickup schedules. Account for weekends and closures, then confirm the resulting order-by dates with your fulfillment partner before publishing them.


### Do fulfillment SLAs change during peak season?


They can, depending on your agreement. Confirm whether processing timelines, volume conditions, cutoffs, or exclusions change during peak. Use those agreed terms when reviewing performance and setting customer expectations.


### Which fulfillment metrics should brands monitor during holiday promotions?


Monitor order volume against forecast, available inventory, unshipped order age, on-time shipping, shipment exceptions, order accuracy, and cost per order. Review carrier delivery performance separately so your team can identify where delays occur and take the right action.
